title: Protect the evaluation boundary
description: Choose what the model must generalize to, select a split, and decide which rows may teach preprocessing state. Watch the held-out evidence become credible or contaminated.

strategies.label: Random row split
strategies.detail: Useful only when rows are independent and the deployment distribution is exchangeable.

strategies.label: Group split
strategies.detail: Keeps every record for one entity on the same side of the boundary.

strategies.label: Chronological split
strategies.detail: Trains on earlier periods and evaluates on later, unseen periods.

fitScopes.label: Training rows only
fitScopes.detail: Fit imputers, scalers, vocabularies, and selectors on train; reuse frozen state elsewhere.

fitScopes.label: All rows before splitting
fitScopes.detail: Held-out distributions influence learned transform state and make evaluation optimistic.

scenarios.label: Independent support tickets
scenarios.context: One row per unrelated ticket; predict routing for another ticket from the same intake process.
scenarios.deploymentQuestion: Can the model route another independent ticket?
scenarios.mismatchRisk: A non-random boundary changes the evaluation population without matching this deployment question.

scenarios.label: Recurring customer behavior
scenarios.context: Several rows describe each customer; predict behavior for a customer the model has never seen.
scenarios.deploymentQuestion: Can the model generalize to a new customer?
scenarios.mismatchRisk: The same customer's history can appear in training and evaluation, rewarding memorization instead of new-customer generalization.

scenarios.label: Future demand forecast
scenarios.context: Rows form a time series; predict a later operating period from information available earlier.
scenarios.deploymentQuestion: Can the model forecast a future period?
scenarios.mismatchRisk: Random assignment lets later conditions enter training while earlier periods remain in evaluation, violating the forecast's time boundary.
